Market context — federal data, not board data

Michigan employs about 18,850 industrial machinery mechanics — a location quotient of 1.57, meaning the occupation is 57% more concentrated here than the U.S. average — at a median wage of $63,030 a year ($30.30 an hour).

Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS), May 2024, for Industrial Machinery Mechanics (SOC 49-9041) in Michigan — the closest federal occupation family to controls work. Two honest comparisons: the trade's statewide workforce is deep and proven, and the pay posted on this board (median $51.44/hr, n = 14) sits above that occupation's median — PLC and controls roles are the premium end of the trade, and Michigan employers are pricing them that way.

Methodology — what this page is, and is not

This snapshot counts job openings indexed from employer postings collected October 26 – November 23, 2026 and live on MI Controls Jobs on November 23, 2026. Every posting was verified live on its posting page; the weekly liveness refreshes (November 2, 9, 16, and 23) removed every posting that could not be verified live, and every addition was verified on its posting page before indexing. Pay figures use only the postings that state parseable pay (n = 14 of 99); annual figures are converted at 2,080 hours and ranges count at their midpoint. Role groupings are made from the postings' own job titles. The federal figures in the market-context box are BLS OEWS estimates, not board data. This page does not count — and does not claim — a candidate pool, a subscriber list, or applicant volume; it is a count of employer demand, published so employers can see the market they are hiring into.
